reason: The cited evidence shows oxide formation (E1) and galvanic corrosion between phases (E3), but none of the passages involve simultaneous wear, so the core premise that wear disrupts the oxide film and triggers the feedback loop is unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: Elevated-temperature corrosion forms protective oxide films (Fe2O3, Cr2O3, Al2O3) on the HEA.
Mechanical wear disrupts and removes these protective oxide films.
Exposed phase boundaries and microstructural heterogeneities promote localized galvanic coupling.
Galvanic coupling accelerates anodic dissolution of susceptible phases.
This creates a synergistic feedback loop accelerating total degradation.
